tagline: Nine miles of Battleground Road, from the town to the field.
intro: SC 110 leaves the town of Cowpens and heads north as Battleground Road, a two-lane country highway with few intersections. The south end near I-85 has gone commercial, and the two counties have a corporate park at their line, but miles three through six pass through farm country with vistas of their own. The road ends beside the battlefield at SC 11, the Cherokee Foothills highway, nine miles on.
Near the north end was Ezell, named for a local merchant, J. H. Ezell, with a post office from 1880 to 1906. It is a ghost town now.

moments.title: Cowpens
moments.text: A town named for the cattle pens near its first site, chartered in 1880, with a depot built in 1896 that is now on the National Register.

moments.title: Cowpens National Battlefield
moments.text: Here on January 17, 1781, Daniel Morgan beat Banastre Tarleton, and the park keeps the rebuilt log cabin of Robert Scruggs, who farmed the ground before it became a park.
